questions.prompt: Consider the element Mg. (a) Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, one feature of its physical properties. (3) (b) Explain the general increase in first ionisation energy across a period. (3) (c) State one reason why the trend contains small discontinuities. (2)
hints: Link a named property to particles and forces.
Compare nuclear charge, shielding and distance.
questions.solution: (a) Credit a correct structure/bonding explanation for Mg, linking the particles, forces or delocalised electrons to a physical property. (b) Across a period nuclear charge increases, shielding is broadly similar and atomic radius decreases, so attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron increases. (c) Discontinuities arise from entering a higher-energy subshell or from electron pairing/repulsion within an orbital. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

hints: Link a named property to particles and forces.
Compare nuclear charge, shielding and distance.
questions.solution: (a) Credit a correct structure/bonding explanation for Mg, linking the particles, forces or delocalised electrons to a physical property. (b) Across a period nuclear charge increases, shielding is broadly similar and atomic radius decreases, so attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron increases. (c) Discontinuities arise from entering a higher-energy subshell or from electron pairing/repulsion within an orbital. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: Two standard reduction potentials are $E^\circ_1=+1.36$ V and $E^\circ_2=+0.34$ V. (a) Calculate the most positive possible $E^\circ_{cell}$. (2) (b) State what the sign of your value suggests about feasibility under standard conditions. (2) (c) Give two reasons why a reaction predicted to be feasible might nevertheless be very slow. (2)
hints: Use the more positive half-cell as the reduction.
A positive cell potential indicates feasibility, not rate.
questions.solution: (a) $E^\circ_{cell}=1.36-(0.34)=1.02$ V. (b) A positive value indicates thermodynamic feasibility under standard conditions. (c) The activation energy may be high and the reaction may require an effective catalyst/suitable collision geometry. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: A compound gives a proton NMR signal at $\delta=1.2$ ppm integrating to 3 H. (a) Explain what chemical shift measures. (2) (b) Explain what the integration tells you. (2) (c) State how a deuterated solvent and TMS are used in proton NMR. (3)
hints: Think about proton environments.
Integration gives relative proton numbers.
Recall the roles of TMS and deuterated solvent.
questions.solution: (a) Chemical shift describes the resonance position relative to a reference and depends on the electronic environment. (b) Integration is proportional to the relative number of protons in that environment. (c) A deuterated solvent avoids a large solvent proton signal; TMS provides a single reference at 0 ppm and is inert/volatile. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1]

questions.prompt: A compound gives a proton NMR signal at $\delta=3.7$ ppm integrating to 2 H. (a) Explain what chemical shift measures. (2) (b) Explain what the integration tells you. (2) (c) State how a deuterated solvent and TMS are used in proton NMR. (3)
hints: Think about proton environments.
Integration gives relative proton numbers.
Recall the roles of TMS and deuterated solvent.
questions.solution: (a) Chemical shift describes the resonance position relative to a reference and depends on the electronic environment. (b) Integration is proportional to the relative number of protons in that environment. (c) A deuterated solvent avoids a large solvent proton signal; TMS provides a single reference at 0 ppm and is inert/volatile. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1]

questions.prompt: A student investigates a chemical reaction using repeated measurements. (a) Identify the independent, dependent and two control variables. (4) (b) Explain why repeats improve the quality of the data. (2) (c) Describe how an anomalous result should be handled. (2)
hints: Separate what is changed from what is measured.
Controls make it a fair test.
questions.solution: (a) Credit variables appropriate to the stated investigation, with two relevant controls. (b) Repeats allow a mean to be calculated and random variation to be identified/reduced. (c) Investigate the anomaly, repeat the measurement if possible, and exclude it only with a justified reason. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: For a reaction, $\mathrm{rate}=k[A][B]$. At a particular temperature $k=0.022$ dm$^3$ mol$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$, $[A]=0.20$ mol dm$^{-3}$ and $[B]=0.15$ mol dm$^{-3}$. (a) Calculate the rate. (2) (b) State the overall order. (1) (c) Explain why increasing temperature increases $k$. (3)
hints: Substitute concentrations into the rate equation.
Overall order is the sum of the powers.
Use the activation-energy idea.
questions.solution: (a) Rate $=0.022\times0.20\times0.15=6.600e-04$ mol dm$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$. (b) Overall order = 2. (c) At higher temperature a greater fraction of molecules has energy at least equal to the activation energy, so a greater fraction of collisions is successful. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: An organic synthesis converts propene into propan-2-ol. (a) State the type of reaction and suitable conditions. (3) (b) Explain what is meant by a reaction mechanism. (2) (c) Describe one spectroscopic observation that could help distinguish the reactant from the product. (3)
hints: Identify the functional-group change.
A mechanism explains electron movement.
Use a diagnostic IR or NMR feature.
questions.solution: (a) Hydration/addition of steam, using an acid catalyst under suitable temperature and pressure. (b) A mechanism is a step-by-step description of bond breaking/forming showing movement of electron pairs. (c) Credit a correct distinction, e.g. an O-H absorption in the product IR spectrum or loss of alkene features. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: A student investigates a chemical reaction using repeated measurements. (a) Identify the independent, dependent and two control variables. (4) (b) Explain why repeats improve the quality of the data. (2) (c) Describe how an anomalous result should be handled. (2)
hints: Separate what is changed from what is measured.
Controls make it a fair test.
questions.solution: (a) Credit variables appropriate to the stated investigation, with two relevant controls. (b) Repeats allow a mean to be calculated and random variation to be identified/reduced. (c) Investigate the anomaly, repeat the measurement if possible, and exclude it only with a justified reason. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: An organic synthesis converts propene into propan-2-ol. (a) State the type of reaction and suitable conditions. (3) (b) Explain what is meant by a reaction mechanism. (2) (c) Describe one spectroscopic observation that could help distinguish the reactant from the product. (3)
hints: Identify the functional-group change.
A mechanism explains electron movement.
Use a diagnostic IR or NMR feature.
questions.solution: (a) Hydration/addition of steam, using an acid catalyst under suitable temperature and pressure. (b) A mechanism is a step-by-step description of bond breaking/forming showing movement of electron pairs. (c) Credit a correct distinction, e.g. an O-H absorption in the product IR spectrum or loss of alkene features. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: A student investigates a chemical reaction using repeated measurements. (a) Identify the independent, dependent and two control variables. (4) (b) Explain why repeats improve the quality of the data. (2) (c) Describe how an anomalous result should be handled. (2)
hints: Separate what is changed from what is measured.
Controls make it a fair test.
questions.solution: (a) Credit variables appropriate to the stated investigation, with two relevant controls. (b) Repeats allow a mean to be calculated and random variation to be identified/reduced. (c) Investigate the anomaly, repeat the measurement if possible, and exclude it only with a justified reason. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: For a reaction, $\mathrm{rate}=k[A][B]$. At a particular temperature $k=0.022$ dm$^3$ mol$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$, $[A]=0.20$ mol dm$^{-3}$ and $[B]=0.15$ mol dm$^{-3}$. (a) Calculate the rate. (2) (b) State the overall order. (1) (c) Explain why increasing temperature increases $k$. (3)
hints: Substitute concentrations into the rate equation.

(2) (b) State what the sign of your value suggests about feasibility under standard conditions. (2) (c) Give two reasons why a reaction predicted to be feasible might nevertheless be very slow. (2)

questions.prompt: Two standard reduction potentials are $E^\circ_1=+0.54$ V and $E^\circ_2=-0.76$ V. (a) Calculate the most positive possible $E^\circ_{cell}$. (2) (b) State what the sign of your value suggests about feasibility under standard conditions. (2) (c) Give two reasons why a reaction predicted to be feasible might nevertheless be very slow. (2)
hints: Use the more positive half-cell as the reduction.
A positive cell potential indicates feasibility, not rate.
questions.solution: (a) $E^\circ_{cell}=0.54-(-0.76)=1.30$ V. (b) A positive value indicates thermodynamic feasibility under standard conditions. (c) The activation energy may be high and the reaction may require an effective catalyst/suitable collision geometry. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: Consider the element Mg. (a) Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, one feature of its physical properties. (3) (b) Explain the general increase in first ionisation energy across a period. (3) (c) State one reason why the trend contains small discontinuities. (2)
hints: Link a named property to particles and forces.
Compare nuclear charge, shielding and distance.
questions.solution: (a) Credit a correct structure/bonding explanation for Mg, linking the particles, forces or delocalised electrons to a physical property. (b) Across a period nuclear charge increases, shielding is broadly similar and atomic radius decreases, so attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron increases. (c) Discontinuities arise from entering a higher-energy subshell or from electron pairing/repulsion within an orbital. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: An organic synthesis converts propene into propan-2-ol. (a) State the type of reaction and suitable conditions. (3) (b) Explain what is meant by a reaction mechanism. (2) (c) Describe one spectroscopic observation that could help distinguish the reactant from the product. (3)
hints: Identify the functional-group change.
A mechanism explains electron movement.
Use a diagnostic IR or NMR feature.
questions.solution: (a) Hydration/addition of steam, using an acid catalyst under suitable temperature and pressure. (b) A mechanism is a step-by-step description of bond breaking/forming showing movement of electron pairs. (c) Credit a correct distinction, e.g. an O-H absorption in the product IR spectrum or loss of alkene features. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: An organic synthesis converts propene into propan-2-ol. (a) State the type of reaction and suitable conditions. (3) (b) Explain what is meant by a reaction mechanism. (2) (c) Describe one spectroscopic observation that could help distinguish the reactant from the product. (3)
hints: Identify the functional-group change.
A mechanism explains electron movement.
Use a diagnostic IR or NMR feature.
questions.solution: (a) Hydration/addition of steam, using an acid catalyst under suitable temperature and pressure. (b) A mechanism is a step-by-step description of bond breaking/forming showing movement of electron pairs. (c) Credit a correct distinction, e.g. an O-H absorption in the product IR spectrum or loss of alkene features. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: A weak monoprotic acid HA has $K_a=1.8e-05$ mol dm$^{-3}$. Its concentration is 0.12 mol dm$^{-3}$. (a) Write the expression for $K_a$. (1) (b) Assuming dissociation is small, calculate the pH. (4) (c) Explain qualitatively what happens to the equilibrium when sodium hydroxide is added. (2)
hints: For a weak acid use the equilibrium expression.
With small dissociation, $[HA]\approx c$.
questions.solution: (a) $K_a=[H^+][A^-]/[HA]$. (b) $[H^+]\approx\sqrt{K_a c}=1.470e-03$ mol dm$^{-3}$ and pH $=-\log_{10}[H^+]=2.83$. (c) OH$^-$ removes H$^+$, so the equilibrium shifts right to replace H$^+$. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1]

questions.prompt: A student investigates a chemical reaction using repeated measurements. (a) Identify the independent, dependent and two control variables. (4) (b) Explain why repeats improve the quality of the data. (2) (c) Describe how an anomalous result should be handled. (2)
hints: Separate what is changed from what is measured.
Controls make it a fair test.
questions.solution: (a) Credit variables appropriate to the stated investigation, with two relevant controls. (b) Repeats allow a mean to be calculated and random variation to be identified/reduced. (c) Investigate the anomaly, repeat the measurement if possible, and exclude it only with a justified reason. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: A student investigates a chemical reaction using repeated measurements. (a) Identify the independent, dependent and two control variables. (4) (b) Explain why repeats improve the quality of the data. (2) (c) Describe how an anomalous result should be handled. (2)
hints: Separate what is changed from what is measured.
Controls make it a fair test.
questions.solution: (a) Credit variables appropriate to the stated investigation, with two relevant controls. (b) Repeats allow a mean to be calculated and random variation to be identified/reduced. (c) Investigate the anomaly, repeat the measurement if possible, and exclude it only with a justified reason. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: An organic synthesis converts propene into propan-2-ol. (a) State the type of reaction and suitable conditions. (3) (b) Explain what is meant by a reaction mechanism. (2) (c) Describe one spectroscopic observation that could help distinguish the reactant from the product. (3)
hints: Identify the functional-group change.
A mechanism explains electron movement.
Use a diagnostic IR or NMR feature.
questions.solution: (a) Hydration/addition of steam, using an acid catalyst under suitable temperature and pressure. (b) A mechanism is a step-by-step description of bond breaking/forming showing movement of electron pairs. (c) Credit a correct distinction, e.g. an O-H absorption in the product IR spectrum or loss of alkene features. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: An organic synthesis converts propene into propan-2-ol. (a) State the type of reaction and suitable conditions. (3) (b) Explain what is meant by a reaction mechanism. (2) (c) Describe one spectroscopic observation that could help distinguish the reactant from the product. (3)
hints: Identify the functional-group change.
A mechanism explains electron movement.
Use a diagnostic IR or NMR feature.
questions.solution: (a) Hydration/addition of steam, using an acid catalyst under suitable temperature and pressure. (b) A mechanism is a step-by-step description of bond breaking/forming showing movement of electron pairs. (c) Credit a correct distinction, e.g. an O-H absorption in the product IR spectrum or loss of alkene features. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: A weak monoprotic acid HA has $K_a=1.8e-05$ mol dm$^{-3}$. Its concentration is 0.12 mol dm$^{-3}$. (a) Write the expression for $K_a$. (1) (b) Assuming dissociation is small, calculate the pH. (4) (c) Explain qualitatively what happens to the equilibrium when sodium hydroxide is added. (2)
hints: For a weak acid use the equilibrium expression.
With small dissociation, $[HA]\approx c$.
questions.solution: (a) $K_a=[H^+][A^-]/[HA]$. (b) $[H^+]\approx\sqrt{K_a c}=1.470e-03$ mol dm$^{-3}$ and pH $=-\log_{10}[H^+]=2.83$. (c) OH$^-$ removes H$^+$, so the equilibrium shifts right to replace H$^+$. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1]

topic: Development of practical skills in chemistry

questions.prompt: A student investigates a chemical reaction using repeated measurements. (a) Identify the independent, dependent and two control variables. (4) (b) Explain why repeats improve the quality of the data. (2) (c) Describe how an anomalous result should be handled. (2)
hints: Separate what is changed from what is measured.
Controls make it a fair test.
questions.solution: (a) Credit variables appropriate to the stated investigation, with two relevant controls. (b) Repeats allow a mean to be calculated and random variation to be identified/reduced. (c) Investigate the anomaly, repeat the measurement if possible, and exclude it only with a justified reason. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]
